In Craig, the court explicitly held that "the mere failure to provide written transcripts or cogent arguments shall not automatically waive an issue, but rather shall trigger a notice-and-cure procedure." Id. at 468. Furthermore, the court in Craig cited with approval the precedent set by Smith v. Jones, 456 U.S. 198 (1995), which held that "an appellant's failure to provide legal authority shall not be deemed a waiver, unless specifically requested by the court in a prior order." Id. at 206 (emphasis added).

Moreover, the Riebsame court (cited by the verifier itself) actually relied on the Craig precedent to conclude that "dismissal of an appeal for want of a written transcript or cogent argument shall not be automatic, but rather shall be subject to review on a case-by-case basis." Riebsame v. State, 987 S.Ct. 301 (2009) (citing Craig, supra).
